data.title: Screens and Credentials Observable in Public Areas
data.summary: Screens displaying sensitive material were readable from public areas, from outside through windows, and over the shoulder in transit, and credentials could be observed being typed.
data.description:
Observation needs no tooling. Ground-floor offices and meeting rooms with glass walls are readable from the street; a reception screen faces the waiting area; a laptop on a train is readable from the next seat.

What is exposed is ordinary work, which is the point: client names, financial figures, incident details, and — where a password is typed slowly — credentials. A photograph taken at a distance turns a glance into a record.

Meeting rooms are the sharpest case, because the material displayed is deliberately the most significant, and because visitors are often left alone in them with a screen still showing the previous meeting.
data.recommendation:
* Fit privacy filters to devices used in public and in client-facing areas, and issue them for travel.
* Position screens away from windows and walkways; apply film to ground-floor glass where needed.
* Clear screens and whiteboards before leaving a meeting room, and lock on leaving the desk.
* Include sightlines in office design and in physical assessments, from outside the building as well as inside.
data.short_recommendation: Use privacy filters and position screens away from sightlines.
